newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus no comment on A3XX partners.
newsitem.headline: Airbus no comment on A3XX partners.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie declined to comment on Monday on a British newspaper report it was hoping to sign a partnership deal within a month with Lockheed Martin and a Korean company on its A3XX large plane project.

The Observer newspaper on Sunday reported Airbus hoped to close a deal with Lockheed and either Korean Air Lines Co or Samsung on partnering its planned A3XX, estimated by Airbus to cost $8 billion in development costs.
"We don't confirm the report," an Airbus spokeswoman said, reiterating that the company was still seeking partners in North America, Europe and Asia.
Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot said on January 13 the company was in talks with Lockheed Martin over possible cooperation on projects, including the A3XX.
Separately, the Airbus spokeswoman said recent comments by Rolls-Royce Plc chairman Ralph Robbins on considering building a new engine for the planned A340-600 were "very encouraging".
Robins told Reuters last Thursday Rolls was actively considering an engine for the stretched version of the long-range plane and there could be more news in the spring or summer.
Aerospatiale is a senior member of the Airbus grouping. Other partners are British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG and Casa of Spain.
Airbus has held discussions with Northrop Grumman about building engine housings for the A3XX but the talks did not lead to an agreement, industry sources said.
In South Korea, both KAL and Samsung firms declined to comment that they were close to signing an agreement, although company officials said they were interested in the project.
Airbus is looking for risk-sharing partners for up to 40 percent of the A3XX, which is expected to be launched in 1998 or early 1999 for entry in service in 2003.
Airbus wants to break Boeing's monopoly of the 400-plus passenger segment with its own product, which would seat 550 and cost $198 million in the basic version.
